question.text: Under the SEBI (SAST) Regulations, the escrow amount that an acquirer must deposit to secure performance of an open offer is computed as:

answer.text: 10% of the total consideration, regardless of size
A flat Rs. 100 crore for every open offer
25% of the consideration on the first Rs. 500 crore, plus 10% on the balance consideration
25% of the total consideration in every case, with no tiered scale

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (SAST) Regulations, the escrow amount is computed on a tiered scale: 25% of the consideration on the first Rs. 500 crore, plus 10% of the balance consideration above Rs. 500 crore. The escrow may be in the form of a cash deposit with a scheduled commercial bank, a bank guarantee, or a deposit of frequently traded securities. The Trap: A common distractor is a flat 25% with a "Rs. 100 crore floor" — there is no such floor in the workbook escrow scale. Equally, a flat 10% or a flat Rs. 100 crore amount ignores the explicit two-tier formula. Note: For conditional offers, the workbook separately requires escrow equal to 100% of the consideration payable for the minimum acceptance level or 50% of the consideration payable under the open offer, whichever is higher.
